manual.title: {{project.name}} Manual
manual.subtitle: Deterministic Esoteric Parlor Orchestration, Apparition Vitrine & One-Finger Accompanist
manual.description: Comprehensive 3x technical manual documenting what each component does, how its execution and audio/visual mechanisms operate, and why it is designed under strict zero-dependency and esoteric computation invariants.

sections.title: Foundations & Architectural Boundaries
sections.description: Core deterministic seed generation, interpreter boundaries, score validation, and zero-dependency guarantees.

entries.title: Phrase Normalization & Deterministic Seed Hashing
entries.summary: Transforms arbitrary human text input into an immutable unsigned 32-bit seed.
entries.what: Accepts user text up to 72 characters, trims surrounding whitespace, collapses internal whitespace sequences into single ASCII spaces, converts text to lowercase, and hashes the normalized string into an unsigned 32-bit integer. Rejects empty phrases or whitespace-only inputs at the boundary.

how.lead: The normalization and hashing pipeline follows a strict pure functional path in `src/score.mjs`:
points: `normalizePhrase()` applies Unicode normalization, lowercasing, and regex space collapsing `s.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`.
`hashPhrase()` executes a 32-bit FNV-1a non-cryptographic dispersion algorithm using offset basis `0x811c9dc5` and prime `0x01000193`.
Bitwise operations (`Math.imul` and `>>> 0`) guarantee that the resulting integer remains unsigned and bit-identical across JavaScript engines on all platforms.

entries.why: A creature's identity depends on exact determinism: confiding identical words must invariably summon the identical specimen. Using FNV-1a on normalized text avoids cross-browser string hashing discrepancies while forgiving accidental double spaces and letter case differences without altering semantics (ADR D-003).

entries.title: LOLCODE 1.2 Interpreted Score Engine
entries.summary: Executes the generative score spell inside a purpose-built in-browser LOLCODE interpreter.
entries.what: Executes `src/oracle.lol` locally in JavaScript. The spell acts as the causal bandleader of the universe: it seeds every visual property, anatomical feature, musical mode, and accompaniment parameter across all six languages, emitting `key=integer` pairs.

how.lead: The interpreter in `src/lolcode.mjs` implements an honest, spec-compliant subset of LOLCODE 1.2:
points: Parses `HAI 1.2` through `KTHXBYE` and manages a dynamic symbol table with lexical scoping.

Executes variable declaration (`I HAS A`), assignment (`R`), math operations (`SUM OF`, `DIFF OF`, `PRODUKT OF`, `QUOSHUNT OF`, `MOD OF`), Boolean logic (`BOTH OF`, `EITHER OF`, `NOT`), condition blocks (`O RLY? / YA RLY / NO WAI / OIC`), switches (`WTF? / OMG / OMGWTF`), loops (`IM IN YR / IM OUTTA YR`), and printing (`VISIBLE`).
Injects the normalized phrase seed as an initial global variable `INPUT_SEED`.
Fails closed with exact line numbers and statement context whenever unsupported syntax or uninitialized variables are encountered.

entries.why: Rather than generating parameters through arbitrary JavaScript math, every creature's soul originates in LOLCODE. Purpose-building the interpreter avoids bundling heavy third-party runtimes, preserves the zero-dependency contract, and guarantees that errors are debuggable with precise line numbers (ADR D-002).

entries.title: Immutable Generative Score Grammar & Allowlist Validation
entries.summary: Validates every output parameter against strict allowable keys and numeric bounds before rendering.
entries.what: Parses raw text emitted by `src/oracle.lol` into an immutable, frozen score object. Ensures that every required field is present exactly once and within valid range bounds, rejecting unknown keys, malformed integers, or missing properties.

how.lead: `parseScore()` in `src/score.mjs` enforces an exhaustive schema check on the spell's key-value lines:
points: Splits stdout into lines, verifies `key=value` format, and rejects duplicates or unauthorized field names.

Validates numerical ranges for visual traits (hue 0..359, size 36..100, shape 0..9, symmetry 2..15, bloom 0..100, edge 0..100, motion 0..100, eyes 1..9, irisStyle 0..7, pupilShape 0..7, irisHue 0..359, eyeLayout 0..5, kineticMode 0..7, kineticSpeed 20..100, kineticDepth 20..100, kineticTilt 0..7, fluxMode 0..7).

Validates numerical ranges for lead audio (pulse 42..167, waveform 0..3, voice 0..5, rhythm 0..5, melodyMode 0..11, melodyTurn 0..11, root 36..60, scale 0..7, gate 40..95) and accompaniment engines (beatMode 0..7, beatDensity 35..100, bassMode 0..7, bassGlide 20..100, harmonyMode 0..7, harmonyStrum 15..100, chimeMode 0..7, chimeShimmer 20..100, chantMode 0..7, chantFormant 25..100).
Composes an evocative multi-tier ceremonial name using seed-driven vocabulary matrices (`THE <ADJECTIVE> <VESSEL> OF <DOMAIN>`).
Returns a deeply frozen `Object.freeze()` score structure.

entries.why: Treating interpreter output as an untrusted boundary prevents corrupted, NaN, or out-of-range values from reaching Web Audio or Canvas. Audio nodes can produce speaker damage or ear injury if fed infinite or NaN frequencies; strict validation guarantees safe audio synthesis and predictable visual framing (ADR D-004).

entries.title: Zero-Dependency & Client-Only Privacy Boundary
entries.summary: Maintains an unyielding guarantee that all computation, rendering, and synthesis occur locally on-device.
entries.what: Executes entirely in modern evergreen web browsers using native HTML5, CSS3, Canvas 2D, and Web Audio APIs. Transmits zero telemetry, analytics, cookies, local storage entries, or network requests after initial static file fetch.

how.lead: The zero-dependency discipline is enforced both architecturally and by automated CI tests:
points: `tests/static.test.mjs` scans all authored source files, asserting that no `http://` or `https://` URLs, external CDN imports, or `node_modules` references exist.

All six esoteric programs (`src/oracle.lol`, `src/beat.mal`, `src/bass.bf`, `src/harmony.bfg`, `src/pad.piet`, `src/chimes.frac`, `src/chant.spl`) are bundled as plain static text files served from the same HTTP origin.
No server-side processing, database, or cloud infrastructure is involved.

entries.why: Privacy, speed, and durability are non-negotiable architectural pillars. Relying on remote servers or third-party CDNs introduces tracking risks, network latency, bit rot, and external failure points. A static zero-dependency toy remains functional indefinitely (ADR D-001).

entries.title: Esoteric Victorian Parlor Cabinet & Broadsheet Styling
entries.summary: Immerses the user in a 19th-century macabre spiritualist chamber and specimen broadsheet.
entries.what: Frames the oracle not as a generic digital app or flat modern widget, but as a centered antique spiritualist cabinet featuring an arched bell-jar apparition vitrine, engraved book-serif typography, telegraph monospace, foxed vellum textures, ebonized wood, and tarnished brass rules.

how.lead: The visual system in `styles.css` builds rich textures entirely through CSS without external image binaries:
points: Employs a high-contrast palette of oxblood (`#6b1f28`), tarnished brass (`#b89249`), bright brass (`#d9b86c`), foxed vellum (`#f4ede2`), and ebonized wood (`#120e0c`).
Uses system book serifs (`Palatino Linotype`, `Book Antiqua`, `Iowan Old Style`, `Georgia`) and telegraph monospace (`Courier New`, `Courier`), avoiding external web font downloads.
Renders ornamental spandrels, astrolabe rings, and eye crests via inline SVGs embedded directly in the markup.
Provides responsive reflow across desktop, tablet, and mobile with accessible touch targets, high contrast, and `prefers-reduced-motion` overrides.

entries.why: Art direction moved decisively away from generic futuristic dark modes or pastel storybooks to a bespoke, eccentric Victorian macabre parlor aesthetic. Using layered CSS gradients and system fonts delivers tactile richness without sacrificing performance or violating zero-dependency boundaries (ADR D-011).

sections.title: Visual Anatomy & Kinetic Apparition (Plate I)
sections.description: Procedural biological forms, dynamic silhouette deformation, rotating 4D tesseract cores, and interactive vitrine gestures.

entries.title: Clamped Kinetic Silhouette & Deforming Boundary Flux
entries.summary: Renders organic, undulating perimeter boundaries clamped strictly within a visible envelope.
entries.what: Computes a continuous closed boundary path for the creature using one of ten base shape archetypes (oval, bell, spindle, tesseract, clover, crescent, lantern, diamond, amphora, scarab) deformed by one of eight seed-selected flux grammars (breathing ripple, traveling peristalsis, nodal pulsation, standing wave, cardioid heartbeat, chaotic flux, twist wave, crystalline facet).

how.lead: `traceBody()` in `src/app.mjs` executes procedural polar coordinate mathematics:
points: Evaluates `points` radial vertices around $2\pi$ radians.
Computes base radius $r(\theta)$ from the creature's shape harmonics and symmetry index.
Applies time-varying flux offsets $\Delta r(\theta, t)$ driven by `elapsed` seconds, flux mode frequency, and interactive touch deformation.
Strictly clamps the normalized radius envelope to $[0.38, 1.08]$ to prevent visual clipping or stage escape.
Applies an isolated radial glow on the body fill pass, then clears `shadowBlur` before kinetic linework to maintain 60 FPS performance.

entries.why: Early prototypes suffered from jittery pulse-dominated blobs that repeatedly broke past canvas boundaries or lagged due to unconstrained shadow blur. Clamping the deformation mathematically and clearing the body glow ensures fluid, organic movement within the bell jar (ADRs D-007, D-008).

entries.title: Bounded Internal Kinetic Systems & 4D Projected Tesseract
entries.summary: Animates independent mathematical motion systems clipped within the deforming creature boundary.
entries.what: Renders one of eight sophisticated kinetic systems moving inside the creature's body: a four-dimensional rotating hypercube (tesseract), orbiting astrolabe rings, concentric hypocycloid gears, phyllotaxis spiral florets, Lissajous harmonograph knots, double pendulum chaos traces, nested chiral polyhedra, or a self-weaving crystal network.

how.lead: `drawKineticCore()` in `src/app.mjs` clips rendering to the active `traceBody()` path:
points: For `drawTesseract()`, defines 16 four-dimensional vertices $(\pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1, \pm 1)$ and 32 connecting edges.
Applies continuous 4D rotation matrices in the $XW$ and $YZ$ planes parameterized by `elapsed * speed`.
Performs two-stage 4D-to-3D-to-2D perspective projection onto the 2D Canvas.
Styles lines with palette-derived semitransparent stroke gradients and dynamic thickness based on touch velocity.

entries.why: Static creatures felt flat and lifeless. Projecting true multidimensional mathematical structures into the clipped interior creates an authentic sense of an ethereal, impossible specimen trapped under glass (ADR D-007).

entries.title: Generative Eye Anatomy, Sclera Silhouettes, & Gaze Tracking
entries.summary: Composes multi-part ocular anatomy with interactive gaze tracking and distinct iris geometries.
entries.what: Generates 1 to 9 distinct eyes possessing unique sclera silhouettes (almond, circle, oval, teardrop, hex, crescent, cat-eye, slit), iris styles (solid, radial, dual-ring, starburst, vortex, eclipse, fractal, nebula), pupil shapes (round, vertical slit, horizontal slit, goat bar, keyhole, diamond, cross, crescent), and autonomous gaze shifts.

how.lead: `drawEye()` in `src/app.mjs` positions eyes according to seed-driven spatial layouts:
points: Places eyes using single-cyclops, bilateral, vertical column, triangular trinity, orbital ring, or scattered cluster arrangements.
Tracks mouse/pointer position when hovering near the vitrine, smoothly interpolating pupil gaze towards the pointer with bounded deflection.
Dilates pupil aperture during vitrine tap and hold gestures.
Applies deterministic iris hue shifts and specular highlights.

entries.why: Repeated, identical stamped eyes made creatures look like mechanical clip art. Giving eyes varied biological silhouettes, layered optical depths, and responsive gaze tracking gives each manifestation a watchful, unsettling personality (ADR D-006).

entries.title: Expressive Touch/Pointer Gestures & Harmonic Field Modulation
entries.summary: Transforms the apparition vitrine into a live expressive performance instrument.
entries.what: Allows the user to tap, hold, and drag directly across the glass vitrine (`#vision`). Gestures trigger synthesized membrane and glass percussion, elastic silhouette deformation, filter sweeps, echo swell, and polar harmonic phase shifting without mutating the underlying deterministic score.

how.lead: Pointer events (`pointerdown`, `pointermove`, `pointerup`) feed an active session state `interaction`:
points: Tapping triggers synthesized multi-partial glass strike plucks and expands shockwave ripples on the vitrine.
Holding swells filter cutoff/resonance, dry/wet mix, echo feedback, and morphs the silhouette toward a secondary shape family.

Dragging maps $(x, y)$ coordinates into polar $(r, \theta)$ via `harmonicField()`, crossfading the creature's motif through a consonant $(\cos\alpha, \sin\alpha)$ harmonic phase shift and three-partial drone choir (`-12`, `-5`, `+7`).
Releasing the pointer smoothly decays all offsets back to resting values via exponential smoothing.

entries.why: A passive generative visualizer grows stale quickly. Letting users directly disturb the apparition turns the parlor vitrine into a musical instrument while preserving the core premise: releasing the glass allows the creature to return to its pure, immutable identity (ADR D-012).

entries.title: Procedural Mycelial Network, Botanical Staging, & Bio-Acoustic Sonification
entries.summary: Simulates living mycelial colonization, Victorian vitrine staging, Haeckel engravings, and bio-acoustic sonification.
entries.what: Simulates a living Victorian botanical specimen rooted in an antique turned-wood mahogany pedestal and fibrous peat substrate. Branching hyphal filaments colonize the vitrine and mature over a 10-second envelope, sprouting eight generative sporophore archetypes (Agaric Cap, Bracket Conk, Coral Clavaria, Bioluminescent Bonnet, Cup Peziza, Morel Honeycomb, Globular Puffball, Hyphal Hydra) etched with Ernst Haeckel lithographic anatomy. Condensation micro-droplets cling to the curved bell jar, while Web Audio synthesizes bio-electric action potentials, guttation droplet chimes, and tactile ballistospore puffs.

how.lead: `buildMycelialNetwork()`, `drawVitrinePedestal()`, `drawGlassCondensation()`, and `scheduleFungalBioStep()` in `src/app.mjs` (with `myceliumEvents()` in `src/mycelium.mjs`) execute botanical synthesis:
points: Renders an antique turned-wood mahogany specimen pedestal with polished brass channel ring and fibrous peat/driftwood substrate mounds grounding hyphal rootlets.
Generates 46 deterministic dew condensation micro-droplets clinging along the curved glass profile of the vitrine bell jar, vibrating on tap gestures and catching specimen bloom.

Etches eight sporophore archetypes with Ernst Haeckel-style lithographic details: radiating lamellae, stippled universal veil verrucae, growth sulci, fimbriate eyelash rims, scalariform alveoli, and aculei teeth.

Gives each sporophore form its own voice (`src/mycelium.mjs`): an AGARIC CAP clicks and drips, a BRACKET CONK knocks like wood, a CORAL CLAVARIA glints in rising glassy trains, a BIOLUMINESCENT BONNET rings slow chords, a CUP PEZIZA bloops, a MOREL HONEYCOMB ticks, a GLOBULAR PUFFBALL breathes soft clouds, and a HYPHAL HYDRA chirps. Hyphae lengthen the spike trains and rotate the patterns, spores thicken the puffs, and bloom tilts every pitch (D-042).
Maintains a 35 to 85 particle ballistospore cloud discharging explosive percussive noise puffs and downward pitch chirps when the vitrine glass is disturbed.

entries.why: Transforms the apparition from a floating geometric shape into a preserved Victorian cryptogamic specimen firmly mounted inside physical glass. Grounding substrate, glass condensation, anatomical lithography, and bio-acoustic sonification produce a multisensory experience of living antique science (ADR D-017, ADR D-018).

sections.title: Generative Music & Lead Melody
sections.description: Web Audio look-ahead synthesis, repeating motif grammars, and live master volume and tempo controls.

entries.title: Look-Ahead Web Audio Transport & Master Volume
entries.summary: Schedules multi-voice polyphony smoothly using a precision look-ahead clock.
entries.what: Executes continuous Web Audio playback using a 90 ms interval timer that schedules audio events 280 ms into the future. Routes all synthesizers through per-voice gain nodes, a shared resonant biquad filter, tempo-synced feedback delay, dynamics compressor, and master volume control.

how.lead: `playScore()` and `scheduleAhead()` in `src/app.mjs` coordinate the audio pipeline:
points: Maintains high-precision Web Audio `context.currentTime` scheduling, preventing timing jitter caused by main-thread UI operations.
Computes rhythmic step durations `unit = 60 / pulse / 2` mapped against score rhythm multipliers.
Manages voice stacks, multi-harmonic drones, resonant envelope filters, and ping-pong feedback delays.
`masterGainFor()` applies a perceptual power curve `(vol / 82)^1.6` with 18 ms ramp smoothing, protected from digital clipping by a pre-output dynamics compressor.

entries.why: Early implementations used fixed-duration playback with `setTimeout`, which drifted, clipped, and stopped abruptly. A continuous look-ahead scheduler with compressor protection enables seamless infinite looping and reliable real-time mixing (ADRs D-005, D-009).

entries.title: Master Transport: Play, Pause, Stop & Hotkeys
entries.summary: Starts, pauses at the last heard step, and stops-and-rewinds the ensemble loop from buttons or the keyboard.
entries.what: A brass transport rail (`#transport-deck`) with PLAY, PAUSE, and STOP · REWIND buttons, a loop position readout (`STEP 05 / 12`), and global hotkeys: `Space` toggles play/pause and `Esc` stops and rewinds to step one. Pause resumes on the next unheard step; mute silences without changing the transport state.

how.lead: `src/transport.mjs` holds the pure state model; `runTransportCommand()` in `src/app.mjs` applies it to audio and the page:
points: `transportReduce()` moves between `stopped`, `playing`, and `paused`, keeping a raw step cursor that is never wrapped to 12, so five- and six-cell rhythm patterns resume in phase.
Each live transport records `audibleStep` when a step actually sounds; pausing resumes after it rather than after the 280 ms look-ahead window, so queued but unheard steps are never skipped.
`stopCurrentSound()` fades the whole output bus, not only the drone mix, so already-scheduled drums and bass stop with the pause.

`transportCommandForKey()` leaves Space alone while typing and on keyboard-focused buttons, checkboxes, and switches, but takes it from a control last focused by a pointer press, so Space after clicking MUTATE pauses instead of mutating again.
Audio runs only while the transport is playing and the bell is unmuted; summon and RESTART THE MELODY both issue `restart`.

entries.why: Basic DAW control is the first step toward a playable synthesizer workstation (roadmap P5-18). Pausing by rebuilding the graph at the saved cursor, instead of suspending the AudioContext, keeps the Fun Machine keyboard auditioning while paused and preserves the single-transport invariant (ADR D-023).

entries.title: Twelve Repeating Motif Families
entries.summary: Maps generative seeds into recognizable, musically coherent 12-note loops.
entries.what: Generates exactly twelve semitone offsets selected from twelve distinct motif families: Major Arpeggio, Minor Arpeggio, Diminished Arpeggio, Augmented Arpeggio, Minor 7th Arpeggio, Ascending Chromatic, Descending Chromatic, Interleaved Chromatic, Circle of Fifths, Whole Tone Stride, Glass Ladder, and Seeded Scale Walk.

how.lead: `melodyFor()` in `src/music.mjs` computes the melodic array:
points: Applies the selected melodic mode and root key offset.
Rotates the 12-note array by `melodyTurn` modulo 12 to provide variety in phrase starting points.
Caches the resulting sequence on the active transport.
Maps notes to audio frequencies via `midiToFrequency(note) = 440 * 2^((note - 69) / 12)`.

entries.why: Purely random note selection sounds like formless computer noise. Human ear recognition requires structured motifs, arpeggios, and stepwise motion. Providing twelve distinct families ensures recognizable thematic identity across creatures (ADR D-010).

entries.title: Real-Time Ensemble Tempo Modulation
entries.summary: Enables interactive speed adjustment across all six instruments without loop interruption.
entries.what: Provides an accessible range slider (`#tempo-bpm`, 36 to 208 BPM) with a live numeric readout. Initialized on summon to the creature's native LOLCODE pulse, adjusting the slider immediately paces upcoming subdivisions across all six esoteric accompaniment engines without audio clicks, while double-clicking restores native speed.

how.lead: `setTempoBpm()` and the look-ahead scheduler in `src/app.mjs` synchronize tempo changes:
points: `setTempoBpm()` clamps the input to $[36, 208]$ BPM and updates `#tempo-value` and `#score-pulse`.
`scheduleAhead()` dynamically evaluates `livePulse = activeTempoBpm || score.pulse` on every scheduling cycle.
Calculates `unit = 60 / livePulse / 2` and assigns step durations `stepDuration = unit * lengthMultiplier` to all active instruments.
Delay line time is bounded to 1.45s to avoid buffer overruns while maintaining smooth acoustic resonance.

entries.why: Different listeners prefer leisurely ambient contemplation (e.g. 50 BPM) or energetic driving pulses (e.g. 140 BPM). Allowing dynamic tempo adjustment while defaulting to the creature's deterministic score gives the user expressive control while preserving specimen identity (ADRs D-005, D-009).

sections.title: The Five Esoteric Accompaniment Plates (Plates I–V)
sections.description: Authentic virtual machine execution across Malbolge, Brainfuck, Befunge-93, Piet, FRACTRAN, and Shakespeare Programming Language.

entries.title: Plate I: Malbolge 1998 59,049-Word Ternary Beat Automaton
entries.summary: Executes authentic Malbolge code on a ternary tape to generate 12-step drum patterns.
entries.what: Executes `src/beat.mal` inside a spec-compliant 1998 Malbolge virtual machine (`src/malbolge.mjs`). Decomposes 12 output bytes into a 12-step 3-trit matrix controlling a synthesized bellows kick, clockwork snare, and escapement chime across eight cadence families, with interactive step cycling and mutation controls.

how.lead: The virtual machine implements Ben Olmstead's 1998 Malbolge specification:
points: Initializes a $3^{10} = 59,049$-word ternary memory tape.
Executes ternary crazy operation `crazy(a, b)` and ternary right rotation `rotr(val)`.
Applies load-time opcode validation `(c + [c]) % 94` and runtime `XLAT2` post-instruction encryption.
Limits execution to a 50-instruction budget to protect browser responsiveness.
Web Audio synthesizes kick (pitch-ramped sine), snare (highpass noise burst), and chime (resonant twin sines).

entries.why: Malbolge is renowned as one of the most notoriously difficult programming languages in history. Writing a genuine deterministic Malbolge program that generates rhythmic trits gives the parlor percussion an authentic esoteric pedigree rather than pseudo-random approximation (ADR D-013).

entries.title: Plate II: Brainfuck 1993 256-Cell Walking Tape Bassline
entries.summary: Drives a 12-cell walking sub-bass and acid-organ ostinato from an executed Brainfuck tape.
entries.what: Executes `src/bass.bf` inside a 1993 Urban Müller Brainfuck interpreter (`src/brainfuck.mjs`). Uses pointer movement, cell addition/subtraction, and `[->+<]` transfer loops across 256 byte cells to generate a 12-cell bass ostinato across eight groove archetypes, featuring portamento slide, cell cycling, and tape-shift controls.

how.lead: `runBrainfuck()` in `src/brainfuck.mjs` executes the 8-command language:
points: Pre-validates matching bracket pairs `[` and `]` at load time, reporting exact line/column offsets on failure.
Executes `>`, `<`, `+`, `-`, `.`, `,`, `[`, and `]` on a `Uint8Array(256)` memory tape with a 4,096-step budget.
Maps tape values into pitch intervals, octave registers, slide flags, and accent levels.
Synthesizes bass tones via a sub-sine oscillator mixed with a portamento-gliding sawtooth routed through a resonant lowpass filter.

entries.why: Brainfuck's single-tape linear memory layout is the ideal computational counterpart to an acoustic walking bassline. Transfer loops naturally create rhythmic bass stepping and scalar walking patterns (ADR D-014).

entries.title: Plate III: Befunge-93 2D Torus Mirror Chord Organ
entries.summary: Voices polyphonic 3-note organ triads from a 2D boustrophedon toroidal playfield.
entries.what: Executes `src/harmony.bfg` inside an 80×25 2D torus Befunge-93 interpreter (`src/befunge.mjs`). Employs directional arrows (`> < ^ v`), `#` bridges, arithmetic, and diagonal mirrors (`\ / / \`) to voice polyphonic 3-note reed-organ and glass-harp triads across eight organ archetypes, with live mirror cycling and deflection controls.

how.lead: `runBefunge()` implements Chris Pressey's 1993 2D grid specifications:
points: Navigates a 2D character grid wrapping toroidally across rows and columns.
Maintains a LIFO operand stack for math, duplicates, swaps, and conditional branching (`_`, `|`).
Outputs pitch classes and strum velocities; `/` triggers ascending harp arpeggios while `\` triggers descending rolls.
Synthesizes 3-voice polyphony through twin triangle and pulse organ oscillators with slight chorus detune.

entries.why: Befunge's two-dimensional playfield and reflective mirrors model physical acoustic reflections and counterpoint. The path of the instruction pointer through 2D space naturally maps to harmonic inversions and strum directions (ADR D-014).

entries.title: Plate IV: Piet Codel Canvas & FRACTRAN Prime-Ratio Spectral Chimes
entries.summary: Drives 7-limit Just Intonation bells and spectral chorus pads from 2D codels and prime fractions.
entries.what: Executes a 49-step 25×5 clockwise Piet 2001 codel canvas (`src/pad.piet`) across all 18 chromatic codels paired with a 12-step 1987 John Conway FRACTRAN prime-ratio program (`src/chimes.frac`) over $2^a 3^b 5^c 7^d 11^e 13^f$. Voices pure 5-limit and 7-limit Just Intonation overtone bells and synesthetic codel-filtered chorus pads across eight archetypes.

how.lead: `src/fractran.mjs` executes both esolangs deterministically:
points: Piet interpreter tracks Direction Pointer (DP) and Codel Chooser (CC) transitions between 6 hues and 3 lightness levels, computing hue and lightness delta commands (`push`, `add`, `roll`, `out`).
FRACTRAN engine multiplies BigInt state $N$ by a sequence of fractions $P_i / Q_i$, finding the first fraction producing an integer and factoring exponents via prime factorization.
Chimes are synthesized as pure non-dispersive sine partials with exponential bell decay.

entries.why: Combining Piet's geometric visual codels with FRACTRAN's pure arithmetic prime ratios directly links visual color to acoustic overtones. Evaluating rational fractions eliminates 12-TET tuning dissonance and produces crystal-clear Just Intonation chimes (ADR D-014).

entries.title: Plate V: Shakespeare Programming Language 3-Act Formant Vowel Choir
entries.summary: Schedules a 3-formant vowel choir from an authentic Elizabethan tragedy script.
entries.what: Executes `src/chant.spl` (`The Oracular Tragedy of the Parlor Glass.`), a 3-Act, 12-Scene Elizabethan drama with four dramatis personae (Hamlet Tenor, Ophelia Soprano, Prospero Basso, Hecate Alto) inside an SPL interpreter (`src/shakespeare.mjs`). Drives a 3-formant ($F_1, F_2, F_3$) parallel bandpass vowel choir across six distinct vowels (`/ɑ/`, `/ɛ/`, `/i/`, `/o/`, `/u/`, `/æ/`), with live scene cycling and recast mutation.

how.lead: `runShakespeare()` interprets the 2001 Jon Åslund and Karl Hasselström specification:
points: Parses character declarations, dramatic entrances/exits (`[Enter Hamlet and Ophelia]`, `[Exeunt]`), and dialogues.
Computes positive and negative poetic valences from noun/adjective combinations (`a noble, charming prince`, `a vile, cursed toad`).
Manages stack pushes and pops via `Remember me` and `Recall` statements.
Formant vowel synthesis routes a sawtooth excitation source through three parallel second-order resonant bandpass filters configured with human vocal tract resonances.

entries.why: The Elizabethan tragic voice provides theatrical gravitas to the parlor seance. Formant synthesis gives the choir unmistakable human phonetic presence without relying on prerecorded audio samples (ADR D-014).

entries.title: Parlor Bandstand Six-Language Jam Console
entries.summary: Coordinates live ensemble mixing, soloing, and synchronized multi-player mutations.
entries.what: Provides an ensemble mixing console (`#bandstand-engine`) coordinating all six esoteric instruments (LOLCODE 1.2, Malbolge 1998, Brainfuck 1993, Befunge-93, Piet 2001 / FRACTRAN 1987, Shakespeare 2001). Offers `FULL ENSEMBLE` engage, `SOLO ORACLE LEAD`, and synchronized `MUTATE ALL PLAYERS` jam controls.

how.lead: `src/app.mjs` manages individual bus gains and group mutations:
points: Maintains separate Web Audio gain busses (`beatBus`, `bassBus`, `harmonyBus`, `chimeBus`, `chantBus`) with 25 ms smooth gain transitions to prevent audio clicks.
`FULL ENSEMBLE` engages all six engines simultaneously with balanced default mix gains.
`SOLO ORACLE LEAD` ramps accompaniment busses to zero while keeping visual step matrices active.
`MUTATE ALL PLAYERS` fires simultaneous re-incantation steps across all five accompaniment plates and triggers the harmonic conductor.

entries.why: Allowing six esoteric languages to run simultaneously is exciting, but listeners need the ability to isolate individual players, hear the solo bandleader, or mutate the entire band in sync without reloading the page (ADR D-014).

entries.title: Eight-Channel Parlor Mixing Console
entries.summary: Gives each of the eight ensemble voices a fader, stereo pan, mute, solo, and live VU meter.
entries.what: A console (`#mixer-engine`) in the Mix wing, between the Bandstand and the parlor room, with eight strips: LEAD (LOLCODE), MANUAL (Fun Machine), PULSE (Malbolge), BASS (Brainfuck), ORGAN (Befunge), CHIMES (Piet/FRACTRAN), CHOIR (Shakespeare), and MYCELIUM (bio-acoustics). Each strip has a vertical fader with a dB readout, a pan slider, M and S switches, and a post-fader VU column with peak hold and clip warning. Plate ENGAGE/SILENCE switches are the same mutes, and WAV exports follow the mix.

how.lead: `src/mixer.mjs` holds the pure console state; `buildEnsembleGraph()` in `src/ensemble.mjs` builds the strips; `updateMixer()` in `src/app.mjs` applies changes:
points: Each bus routes through a 2-channel `GainNode` fader and a `StereoPannerNode`; upmixing first lets a centered pan pass mono voices at unity.
`channelSettings()` turns faders, pans, mutes, and solos into per-strip gain and pan; any solo isolates the soloed channels, and an explicit mute still wins.
The fader taper is square-law `(v / 80)²` below unity and linear in dB above it, so 40 is −12 dB, 80 is unity, and 100 is +12 dB; changes ramp over a 20 ms time constant.
Live strips carry a post-pan `AnalyserNode`; a `requestAnimationFrame` loop turns `meterReading()` RMS and peak into meter fills with fast attack, a slow fall, and a 0.9 s peak hold.

Each strip opens with a fixed voicing trim from `CHANNEL_VOICING_DB` before its fader (lead +6 dB, choir +12 dB), so the default balance favors the melody and voices while every fader still reads 0.0 dB. A `Math.SQRT1_2` trim on the vitrine drag panner keeps its path at the pre-mixer level.

entries.why: Players asked to balance the six-language band and hear one bandmate at a time (roadmap P5-19). Building the strips into the shared graph means live playback, WAV export, and the planned stem export (P5-21) all hear the same mix. Folding plate switches into mixer mutes leaves one mute per bandmate instead of two that could disagree (ADR D-024).

sections.title: Harmonic & Rhythmic Synchronization (src/conductor.mjs)
sections.description: Pure mathematical harmonization uniting six chaotic esoteric engines into consonant chamber music.

entries.title: Neo-Riemannian Tonnetz Triadic Progression
entries.summary: Organizes the 12-step bar into four parsimonious triadic regions sharing common tones.
entries.what: Generates a 4-region, 12-step harmonic spine using Hugo Riemann's Neo-Riemannian *Tonnetz* operations: Parallel (**P**), Leading-Tone (**L**), and Relative (**R**) involutions. Each step transition preserves exactly two common pitch classes and moves the remaining voice by 1 or 2 semitones.

how.lead: `buildTonnetzSpine()` and `applyTonnetzOperation()` in `src/conductor.mjs` construct the chord progression:
points: Calculates the tonic triad root and quality (`major` or `minor`) from score melody mode and scale.
Executes geometric involutions: **P** toggles major/minor; **L** swaps the root for a leading tone; **R** shifts to the relative major/minor.
Generates 4 harmonic regions of 3 steps each (steps 0..2, 3..5, 6..8, 9..11).
Supplies the active triad (root, third, fifth, seventh, ninth) to guide all instrument voicing.

entries.why: Independent virtual machines generating raw numbers simultaneously produce dissonant tone clusters. Neo-Riemannian voice leading creates rich, cinematic chord progressions that sound mysterious and coherent while allowing esoteric programs to retain their native rhythms (ADR D-016).

entries.title: Leonhard Euler's 1739 Gradus Suavitatis Consonance Sieve
entries.summary: Quantifies interval consonance mathematically to snap melodies and basslines onto consonant chord tones.
entries.what: Computes Leonhard Euler's 1739 *Gradus Suavitatis* (degree of agreeableness) $G(n) = 1 + \sum e_i (p_i - 1)$ over frequency ratios. Snaps strong-beat LOLCODE lead notes, Brainfuck bass roots/fifths, Befunge-93 chord inversions, and Shakespeare formant choir lines onto the most consonant available pitch classes.

how.lead: `eulerGradus()` and `projectConsonantPitch()` in `src/conductor.mjs` evaluate harmonic tension:
points: Calculates prime factorizations of interval fractions $p/q$, evaluating prime penalties for factors 2, 3, and 5.

Unison (1:1) yields degree 1; Octave (2:1) yields degree 2; Perfect Fifth (3:2) yields degree 4; Perfect Fourth (4:3) yields degree 5; Major Third (5:4) yields degree 7; Tritone (45:32) yields degree 14.
`projectConsonantPitch()` finds the candidate note minimizing pitch distance and Euler Gradus score relative to the active Tonnetz triad.
Strong beats (0, 3, 6, 9) require strict triad chord tones, while weak subdivisions permit consonant color extensions (9th, 4th, 6th, 7th).

entries.why: Hard-coding scale presets destroys the authenticity of esoteric VM execution, but unguided output is discordant noise. Euler's 1739 formula provides an objective, historic mathematical sieve that sculpts raw VM output into pure consonant intervals without discarding program logic (ADR D-016).

entries.title: E. Bjorklund's Euclidean Rhythm Hocketing
entries.summary: Interlocks lead, chimes, choir, and percussion into complementary rhythmic pockets.
entries.what: Applies E. Bjorklund's 2003 Euclidean algorithm $E(k, n)$ to distribute $k$ pulses across $n=12$ steps as evenly as possible. Creates interlocking hockets between the LOLCODE lead, Malbolge kick, Piet/FRACTRAN chimes, and Shakespeare vowel choir so voices breathe in complementary pockets.

how.lead: `bjorklund()` in `src/conductor.mjs` generates cyclic binary timing masks:
points: Computes Bresenham-like recursive pulse distributions $E(7, 12)$ for lead melody and $E(5, 12)$ for spectral chimes.
Rotates masks based on score turn fields to vary downbeat syncopation.
Locks Brainfuck bass downbeats to Malbolge kick pulses on step 0 of each 3-step harmonic region.
Suppresses chime and choir triggers when lead notes occupy the subdivision, creating acoustic space for each voice to ring clearly.

entries.why: When six instruments trigger on every 16th-note subdivision simultaneously, the sonic result is a wall of rhythm mud. Euclidean hockets distribute pulses with maximal mathematical spacing, creating infectious polyrhythmic grooves where each instrument has room to be heard (ADR D-016).

entries.title: Kapellmeister Music-Theory & Genre Rulebook Console
entries.summary: Enables real-time switching between seven music-theory rulebooks with live harmonic readouts.
entries.what: Allows the user to select and manipulate the harmonic rulebook governing the six-language esoteric ensemble (`#kapellmeister-engine`). Offers thirteen rulebooks, grouped into families in the menu: Victorian Neo-Riemannian Tonnetz, 12-Bar Delta & Parlor Blues, Smoky Parlor Jazz, Palestrina Modal Counterpoint, Mystic Modal Drone, Parlor Ragtime & Cakewalk Strains (a Joplin-style strain with an oom-pah stride bass, added purely in Inform 7), Doo-Wop Parlor Ballad, Sacred Harp Shape-Note Hymnody, Andalusian Flamenco Cadence, Klezmer Freygish Dance, Sea Shanty & Hornpipe, Silent-Film Lydian Dream (the six of D-041 wave 1, also written only in Inform 7), and Raw Esoteric Chaos. Each creature varies its genre's changes by the moves that genre's rulebook permits (rotation, relative and tritone substitutions, secondary dominants, modal borrowing, cadences, harmonic pace), chosen by the creature's own harmony fields (D-043), so no two creatures need share a progression. The VARIATION line names those moves, and AS WRITTEN switches them off. The harmony moves on a four-pass clock (D-044): each chord holds a whole loop and changes on its downbeat, the readout shows the step and the pass (05 / 12 · 3/4), and the compass lights the pass that is playing. THE CREATURE'S OWN, first in the menu and the rulebook a fresh creature opens in, is a rulebook each creature writes from its own scale through a functional grammar in Inform 7 (tonic, predominant, and dominant regions, and chord shapes tried in order), in the character of a genre it borrows. Displays active Step (01..12), Chord Name (e.g. C Maj, F7, Cmaj9), Harmonic Vector, and Euler Consonance score in real time alongside an interactive SVG Tonnetz compass.

how.lead: `src/rulebooks.ni` states the genres; `src/conductor.mjs` and `src/app.mjs` apply them and show harmonic telemetry:
points: Each genre is written in Inform 7 in `src/rulebooks.ni` (D-033): `buildGenreSpine()` reads its changes table (I7-IV7-V7, Imaj9-vi9-ii9-♭II7alt, suspensions with a Picardy third, root/fifth drone ladders) or walks the Tonnetz, and the menu, title, and motto are built from the same file.
`projectConsonantPitch()` adapts to genre rules: blue-note sieve for blues, guide-tone approach for jazz, and stepwise conjunct motion for counterpoint.
The Euler consonance strictness slider modulates the maximum permissible Gradus threshold from strict (G ≤ 5) to permissive (G ≤ 14).
`highlightBeatStep()` updates the live readout on each 16th-note step and highlights the active region on the SVG Tonnetz compass.

entries.why: Different listeners enjoy different musical aesthetics—from tight contrapuntal elegance to smoky blues to raw, unfiltered avant-garde noise. Exposing the Kapellmeister console puts harmonic mastery directly in the user's hands without destroying the genuine execution of the underlying esoteric programs (ADR D-019).

entries.title: Discovery Drawers & the Whole Cabinet
entries.summary: A first visit opens on a small playable instrument; the Kapellmeister, Mix, Keep, and Band drawers open themselves as the visitor plays.
entries.what: The page starts in discovery: the phrase box, the vitrine, the transport, and the Fun Machine are open, and four drawers wait below with a one-line invitation each. Holding a Fun Machine key wakes the Kapellmeister, finishing a loop opens the Mix, changing something worth keeping opens Keep, and soloing or silencing a voice (or four loops) opens The Band. OPEN THE WHOLE CABINET lays every control bare.

how.lead: `src/cabinet.mjs` holds the state and rules; `src/app.mjs` adds the drawer chrome around existing elements:
points: `cabinetReduce()` applies unlock, toggle, and mode events: a trigger opens a drawer only the first time, and a drawer the visitor closes stays closed.
Sealed drawer bodies use `hidden`, leaving the tab order and the accessibility tree (55 tab stops at first instead of 172); openings are announced through a polite status region without moving focus.
The mode and drawers are remembered in `localStorage` (`edmark-fun-machine.cabinet.v1`), validated by `parseCabinetState()`; without scripts every drawer simply stays open.

entries.why: Fifteen panels of esoteric machinery at once overwhelmed newcomers and keyboard and screen-reader users alike. Discovery lets the depth arrive as the visitor plays, and the whole cabinet keeps everything one switch away (D-037).

entries.title: Inform 7 Kapellmeister Rulebooks
entries.summary: The seven genres are written in a strict subset of Inform 7 and compiled at load into the data the conductor plays.
entries.what: `src/rulebooks.ni` states everything a Kapellmeister genre decides, in Inform 7's English: its chord colours, changes, Fun Machine progressions, melody snapping, bass walk, organ voicing, chime overtones, menu title, and motto. `src/inform.mjs` reads it, rejects anything outside the subset with a line number, and compiles it into frozen genre data before the app plays a note.

how.lead: A purpose-built interpreter for the subset (D-033):
points: Kinds, values, properties with defaults, either/or adjectives (`Delta Blues is an insistent voiced genre.`), globals that vary, tables with `--` blanks and `(continued)`, and genre-based rulebooks that produce values.

Rules such as `Colouring rule for Smoky Parlor Jazz when the interval above the tonic is listed in {0, 5}: rule succeeds with result maj9.` fire in source order, first match wins (a documented departure from Inform's specificity ordering).

`compileRulebooks()` follows every rulebook over its whole domain (12 intervals, strictness 1–14), so playing never runs Inform. The true algorithms a genre names (Tonnetz walking, Euler sieving, contrary motion, cell choosing, inverted triads) stay in `src/conductor.mjs`.
The app installs the compiled rulebooks before anything reads a genre: the Kapellmeister menu, the Fun Machine's key colours, the conductor, and session presets.
`tests/fixtures/rulebooks-golden.json` froze every genre decision before the migration, and the conductor still reproduces it exactly.

entries.why: The genres are the project's most-edited musical knowledge. As English prose and tables they read like a music-theory notebook, and adding or retuning a genre no longer means editing six JavaScript functions. Inform 7's kinds, tables, and rulebooks already had the right shape (D-033).

evidence.label: A test-only genre in Inform 7 alone

entries.title: Antique Parlor Room Acoustic Space & Phonograph Ambience
entries.summary: Synthesizes authentic 1890s Edison cylinder crackle, wood-and-velvet chamber convolution reverb, and clockwork escapement ticking.
entries.what: Embeds the synthetic chamber ensemble into an authentic 1890s Victorian parlor acoustic environment (`#parlor-acoustics-engine`). Combines procedural wax-cylinder surface crackle and horn bandpass resonance, a 1.6-second wood-and-velvet chamber convolution reverb, and brass grandfather clock escapement ticks on quarter-beats, captured faithfully in live Web Audio and offline 16-bit WAV loop exports.

how.lead: `src/app.mjs` procedurally generates the acoustic space using Web Audio API nodes:
points: `ensureWaxCrackleBuffer()` generates a 3.0s stereo buffer synthesizing acoustic recording horn resonance (350–3200 Hz bandpass), Poisson-distributed dust pops, and 78 RPM turntable groove rumble.

`ensureParlorImpulseResponse()` generates a 1.6s stereo impulse response modeling discrete early reflections (12–98 ms) and high-frequency velvet drape absorption for a Web Audio `ConvolverNode`. Every voice but the bass is heard in the room, post-fader (the pulse at half strength), sitting about 14–21 dB under the mix at the default ambience (D-034).
Levels per unit of the ambience slider live in `src/ensemble.mjs`: `PARLOR_REVERB_PER_LEVEL` (1.0) and `PARLOR_CRACKLE_PER_LEVEL` (0.21, halved after listening found the crackle overpowering).

`scheduleClockworkTick()` synthesizes mechanical brass escapement clicks on quarter-beats (steps 0, 3, 6, 9) with high 'tick' (2600 Hz) and lower 'tock' (1800 Hz) transients and a wooden case knock, loud enough to read through the band (peaks near the mix's).
`exportSpecimenWav()` incorporates the identical crackle, chamber convolution, and clockwork escapement ticks into rendered 16-bit PCM WAV loops.

entries.why: Pure mathematical synthesis sounds dry, clinical, and artificial without physical acoustic grounding. Wrapping the esoteric instruments in an authentic 1890s Edison cylinder parlor chamber binds disparate synthesizers into a believable acoustic space with zero external audio assets (ADR D-019).

entries.title: Edmark's Esoteric Fun Machine One-Finger Accompanist
entries.summary: Hold one key and a synth pad plays a swell, arpeggio, or progression in the band's rhythm while the band follows your chord.
entries.what: A 13-key manual (`C..C'`) and computer keys (`[A..K]`) drive a one-finger accompanist inspired by Baldwin home organs, without sounding like one. Hold a key and choose a style chip: SWELL holds one pad chord on the key, ARPEGGIO ripples its tones two per step, PROGRESSION walks the genre's four-chord progression with a singing lead line. The band is re-conducted onto the chord while the LOLCODE lead steps back. (A 12-step punch-in sequencer was removed in D-038; a loop machine is planned as P5-26.)

how.lead: `src/accompaniment.mjs` turns a key into a performance; `src/app.mjs` voices and schedules it on the band's grid:
points: `buildPerformance(key, style, genre, tonic)` returns four region chords and twelve steps; the genre colours each chord through `buildFunChord(key, "auto", …)`.

`schedulePadChord()` plays the chord in the current voice: a validated patch from `src/voices.mjs` (D-040). By default that is THE CREATURE'S OWN: `creatureVoice()` takes the preset the spell's `fun_voice` names, tilts its filters by `fun_bright`, and spreads its detune and width by `fun_spread`. The VOICE chips also offer seven presets (VELVET PAD, HARMONIUM, GLASS HARMONICA, THEATRE ORGAN, STRING MACHINE, MUSIC BOX, ÆTHER CHOIR), whose patches may add a tremolo, formant bands, or a struck, rolled chord. The default, VELVET PAD, is two saws detuned ±8 cents and a triangle under a slowly opening lowpass, with an attack scaled to the chord's length and a release that crossfades into the next. `padVoicing()` voice-leads each change.

`scheduleArpNote()` plucks `arpeggioNotes()` two per step in each step's real duration; `scheduleFunLeadNote()` glides between progression notes with late-arriving vibrato. The Fun Machine strip feeds the delay and chamber reverb.

A held key calls `applyEnsembleConductor()` with the performance's chords converted by `toTonicRelative()`, so the band plays the pad's chord in the right key, and ducks the LOLCODE lead and drones by 10 dB until release.

entries.why: The maintainer wanted pressing a key to feel like a composer leading a band, not like playing a combo organ. Playing on the band's own rhythm and room, re-conducting the band to the held chord, and letting the lead step back makes the player's part the lead (ADR D-029).

evidence.label: Fun Machine voice patches and synths

entries.title: INTERCAL 1972 Grand Ensemble Conductor & Dynamic Arrangement Orchestrator
entries.summary: Master conductor virtual machine executing src/conductor.i to orchestrate dynamic sectional breathing, politeness-checked consonance, and COME FROM turnaround cadences.
entries.what: Overcomes the ensemble's continuous wall of sound by executing a purpose-built 1972 INTERCAL interpreter across the 12-step loop. Uses canonical Woods & Lyon mechanics (PLEASE DO politeness quotient, PLEASE IGNORE / REMEMBER variable masks, and COME FROM cadence interceptions) to dynamically orchestrate channel breathing across Exposition, Antiphony, Tutti, and Breakdown sections.

how.lead: `src/intercal.mjs` and `src/conductor.i` execute genuine INTERCAL 1972 rules:
points: Statement Politeness Checking: enforces the INTERCAL 1972 politeness rule (0.20 <= P/N <= 0.334), rejecting impolite programs with ICL079 and groveling programs with ICL099. The conductor score executes with 8 polite statements out of 35 (22.9%).

Per-phrase form: the host avalanche-mixes the score seed into a 16-bit arrangement word, and `DO WRITE IN .5` / `.6` read it and its complement. Seven select (~) choices then decide who colours the opening, who answers the choir, what sits under the breakdown, and whether the turnaround (`#3 $ .7`, a mingle) starts on step 10 or 11. Guardrails keep at least five band voices on every step and pulse and bass under the first three sections (D-032).

Registers are the arrangement: twospot registers :1..:8 hold one channel each (#1 plays, #0 rests), `.1 <- #n` opens section n (Exposition, Antiphony, Tutti, Breakdown), and the VM snapshots the registers at each marker, so the program itself decides who plays. Malformed form is rejected at summon.
`PLEASE IGNORE :8` freezes the Fun Machine register, so the breakdown's `DO :8 <- #0` does nothing and the player is never rested.
`COME FROM (60)` Turnaround Cadence: `.3` starts the turnaround on step 10 or 11 and COME FROM skips the lead's exit, so pulse, bass, and lead come home through the loop's end.
IntercalVM bitwise operations: supports authentic 16-bit and 32-bit registers, bitwise mingle ($) and select (~), statement labels, and GIVE UP termination.
The workstation shows the form: the transport names the section, console strips light TACET while rested, MIDI exports carry section Marker events, and the stem README lists section times.

entries.why: In real ensemble performance, musicality requires breathing space, call-and-response dynamics, and sectional contrast rather than an unceasing wall of sound where every instrument blasts at maximum density on every step (ADR D-028).

evidence.label: Architecture Records D-028, D-030, D-031, and D-032

sections.title: Specimen Sharing & High-Resolution Broadsheets
sections.description: Privacy-preserving URL fragment sharing and 1200×1520 engraved Victorian broadsheet PNG export.

entries.title: Client-Only #omen=... URL Fragment Sharing
entries.summary: Shares exact specimen links via URL hash fragments without transmitting phrases to servers.
entries.what: Encodes the confidant's phrase into the browser location hash (`#omen=<encoded_phrase>`). Enables one-click link copying (`COPY OMEN LINK`), live address bar synchronization, and instant specimen restoration on link visit or `hashchange` without transmitting data over HTTP request headers.

how.lead: `src/share.mjs` handles hash encoding and restoration:
points: `encodeOmenHash()` percent-encodes normalized phrases into `#omen=...` format.
`decodeOmenHash()` extracts and decodes phrases, ignoring foreign hash targets.
`showScore()` synchronizes browser address bar state via `history.replaceState(null, '', nextHash)`.
When opened from a shared link, the application restores the score immediately while holding audio in suspension until the user clicks Summon, Replay, or Unmute, respecting browser autoplay policies.

entries.why: Traditional web apps use `?query` parameters, which transmit sensitive user input in plain text to web servers, CDN access logs, and HTTP `Referer` headers. RFC 3986 URL fragments (`#`) are processed exclusively on the client, guaranteeing 100% privacy for confidences (ADR D-015).

entries.title: 1200×1520 Engraved Broadsheet Specimen PNG Export
entries.summary: Renders an archival Victorian specimen plate combining live portrait capture, phrase, and ensemble telemetry.
entries.what: Composites an archival 1200×1520 pixel engraved Victorian specimen broadsheet on an offscreen `<canvas>` (`ENGRAVE PNG PLATE`). Downloads the image as `hai-oracle-<name>-<seed>.png`, featuring the live apparition portrait, specimen name, confided phrase, hexadecimal seed, and six-language ensemble telemetry ledger.

how.lead: `renderSpecimenBroadsheetCanvas()` in `src/app.mjs` builds the plate from vector primitives:
points: Fills aged parchment background with double oxblood and brass framing rules and corner rosettes.
Draws typographical masthead, specimen name, and wrapped quotation of the confided phrase.
Captures the live apparition vitrine from `#vision` into an arched bell-jar illustration frame with astrolabe corner spandrels.
Inscribes full ensemble telemetry: hexadecimal seed, LOLCODE score attributes, and executed instruction counts across Plates II through VI.
`exportSpecimenPng()` triggers an immediate browser file download via a temporary data anchor.

entries.why: Users love collecting and saving their discoveries. Rather than downloading a generic square icon, generating a high-resolution 1200×1520 Victorian natural history broadsheet turns every summoned creature into a framed work of art suitable for printing or archival collection (ADR D-015).

entries.title: 16-Bit Uncompressed Deterministic WAV Audio Export
entries.summary: Renders and exports a broadcast-quality 16-bit 44.1 kHz WAV recording of the chamber ensemble loop.
entries.what: Generates a deterministic, uncompressed 16-bit stereo 44.1 kHz PCM WAV recording of the complete 12-step esoteric chamber ensemble loop (`RECORD WAV LOOP`). Uses the browser-native `OfflineAudioContext` and a dependency-free pure JavaScript RIFF/WAVE encoder (`audioBufferToWavBlob()`) to synthesize and download `hai-oracle-<name>-<seed>.wav` in under 60 milliseconds on-device.

how.lead: `exportSpecimenWav()` in `src/app.mjs` and `audioBufferToWavBlob()` in `src/share.mjs` execute offline audio synthesis and PCM packaging:
points: Calculates precise loop duration from active tempo BPM and score rhythm multipliers, adding a 1.35-second tail for delay and reverb decay.

Instantiates a 2-channel 44.1 kHz `OfflineAudioContext` and builds the same graph as live playback with `buildEnsembleGraph()` from `src/ensemble.mjs`, so the export renders the listener's exact routing (ADR D-023).
Schedules all six conducted esoteric instruments (LOLCODE lead, Malbolge beat, Brainfuck bass, Befunge-93 organ, Piet/FRACTRAN chimes, Shakespeare choir) plus fungal bio-acoustics.
`audioBufferToWavBlob()` constructs a canonical 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header and writes interleaved clamped 16-bit signed integer samples.
Triggers immediate browser download via an ephemeral object URL anchor with automatic cleanup.

entries.why: Confidants wanted high-fidelity audio keepsakes of their summoned creatures. Offline Web Audio rendering guarantees bit-exact acoustic determinism without server roundtrips, network telemetry, or heavyweight external audio libraries (ADR D-018).

entries.title: Nine-Stem WAV Bundle & Type 1 MIDI Score
entries.summary: Exports every channel as an aligned WAV stem in one ZIP, and the whole loop as a multi-track MIDI file.
entries.what: `EXPORT 9 STEMS (ZIP)` downloads `…-stems.zip` holding eight channel stems (lead, manual, pulse, bass, organ, chimes, choir, mycelium), a parlor-room stem of crackle and clockwork, and a README with tempo and loop length. `WRITE MIDI SCORE` downloads a Standard MIDI File (Type 1) with a tempo track and seven named instrument tracks, ready to drop into any DAW.

how.lead: `renderEnsembleLoop()` in `src/app.mjs` drives both exports through the shared graph; `src/zip.mjs` and `src/midi.mjs` write the files:
points: Each channel stem renders the loop with only that strip open at its fader and pan (`stemSettings()`), mute and solo ignored, keeping its own chamber reverb; the room stem renders with every strip closed.
`createStoredZip()` writes STORED entries with CRC-32 and the DOS epoch date, so the same stems always make the same archive, and rejects path-traversal entry names.
During a schedule-only pass, each pitched scheduler records its note through `logNote()`, so MIDI comes from the code that makes the sound.

`buildMidiFile()` writes 480 PPQ tracks with General MIDI programs (drums on channel 10), clips notes to the loop, trims overlapping repeats, merges unisons, and scales velocity from each part's loudest event. `funVoiceTracks()` gives each Fun Machine voice in the loop its own MANUAL track, channel, and program, so stacked layers in different voices open as separate instruments.

entries.why: Players wanted to carry a creature into a real studio (roadmap P5-21). Rendering through the shared graph means stems sound exactly like their channel in the mix; capturing notes from the schedulers keeps MIDI from drifting away from the audio. Both writers are a few hundred lines of browser-native code, keeping the zero-dependency boundary (ADR D-025).

entries.title: Session Ledger: On-Device Presets & .fun Files
entries.summary: Saves and restores the whole apparatus as named browser presets or portable session files.
entries.what: The ledger (`#session-engine`) captures the phrase, every plate's mutation count and cell edits, the Fun Machine accompaniment style and voice and its loop-machine song, every recorded slot keeping the voice it was played in (format v6, with the AS WRITTEN switch; older files open in VELVET PAD and as written), the Kapellmeister rulebook and strictness, the parlor room, tempo, master volume, and the full mixing console. `SAVE PRESET` keeps it under a name in this browser only; `SAVE .FUN FILE` and `OPEN .FUN FILE` move it between machines.

how.lead: `src/session.mjs` defines and validates the format; `captureSession()` and `applySession()` in `src/app.mjs` read and restore live state:
points: Sessions are versioned JSON; `validateSession()` requires every field, refuses unknown and prototype keys, range-checks integers, checks enums, and limits files to 64 KB, rejecting a bad file whole and naming the field.
Chords are stored as `(root, quality)` and rebuilt by `buildFunChord()`; plate edits are per-cell click counts replayed through each plate's cycler, since cells cycle independently.
Restoring re-summons the phrase through the normal score path, then layers plates, progression, rulebook, room, tempo, volume, and console, restarting a playing loop.
Presets live in one `localStorage` key, revalidated on every read; every storage call is wrapped so blocked storage falls back to files.

entries.why: A jam that vanishes with the tab is hard to build on (roadmap P5-20). Keeping presets on the device and moving everything else through player-held files preserves the client-only privacy model, and a strict allowlist keeps a shared file from steering the score, audio graph, or page (ADR D-026).
